outcomeNote: Mishna analogy; R' Yehuda extends it

segments.he: מַתְנִי' נָשִׁים בִּבְתוּלֵיהֶם כִּגְפָנִים, יֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ אָדוֹם, וְיֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ שָׁחוֹר, וְיֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ מְרוּבֶּה, וְיֵשׁ גֶּפֶן שֶׁיֵּינָהּ מוּעָט. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל גֶּפֶן יֵשׁ בָּהּ יַיִן, וְשֶׁאֵין בָּהּ יַיִן — הֲרֵי זֶה דּוֹרְקְטִי.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «Women, with regard to» the blood that flows when «their hymens» are ruptured, «are like grapevines: There is a vine that» produces «wine» that «is red, and there is a vine that» produces «wine» that «is black; and there is a vine that» produces «wine in abundance, and there is a vine that» produces only «a meager» amount of «wine. Rabbi Yehuda says: In every vine, there are» grapes fit to produce «wine, but» any vine in «which there are no» grapes fit to produce «wine, this is a dry vine [durkati].» Likewise, any woman who experiences bleeding is capable of giving birth, whereas one who does not experience bleeding is like a dry vine, unable to give birth.

moves.summary: Women's blood varies like vines' wine
Every vine has wine; one without is a dry vine

positions.claim: women differ in colour and quantity of blood as vines differ in wine
every vine has wine; one without is a dry vine (a woman without blood cannot bear)

unresolved.issue: R' Yehuda's clause read as an extension of the analogy (biur: ועוד בהשוואה זו), not a dispute; no disputes_with emitted
